book.title: Competing Against Luck
book.author: Clayton M. Christensen, Taddy Hall, Karen Dillon and David S. Duncan

predict.question: B faces task X 80% of the time and scores 18 there, versus 2 on task Y. What is B’s toy result?

exploreHint: Run both cases; compare the changed input.
bookIdea: Competing Against Luck frames product choice around the progress someone seeks in a particular circumstance.
modelBoundary: A scores {A}; B scores {B}. The product is unchanged; its 18-point fit matters more when task X occurs four times as often. Task frequencies and fit points are stipulated, not measured preferences or a choice law.
doesItHoldUp: Does it hold up? The arithmetic follows our assumptions; real-world applicability and book attribution remain unverified.
